text.title: Futures slip as Nvidia CEO exit hits AI stocks; Nasdaq 100 leads declines
text.summary: US futures point lower, with Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.2% and S&P 500 futures down 0.5%, as Nvidia's fallout weighs on AI-linked tech. Dow futures are nearly flat (-0.1%). Last week's session ended mixed, with the Nasdaq down 0.9%, the S&P 500 down 0.4% and the Dow up 0.1%. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5 bp Friday to 5.15%, and the VIX is at 20.6.

drivers.h: Nvidia CEO exit weighs on AI
drivers.t: Nvidia was down 2.7% in premarket trading after Jensen Huang's resignation, having been down nearly 4% earlier. The FT reports CoreWeave down 8%, and futures are sliding as Nvidia leads AI stocks lower.
Nvidia received two more price target cuts following Huang's departure, ahead of its earnings. Colette Kress is set to give her first earnings call as interim CEO.

Huang's exit has renewed scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's ties to the chipmaker. Singapore and the US also agreed to keep discussing Megaspeed as the Nvidia scandal widens. Chip tensions loom over the Trump-Xi summit.
WTI is down 1.0% at $87.69 as traders weigh signs of a global supply surplus against renewed Middle East attacks and threats to oil shipments.
Bitcoin is down 1.9% at about $64,094. WSJ says bitcoin and ether are trading below key levels as risk appetite remains constrained.
Morgan Stanley raised global equities to 'maximum overweight', citing cheap valuations and earnings strength. That stands against the tech weakness this morning.
